_comment: PEAK and AVERAGE current drawn from the vdd RAIL, per PVT point.
WHY THIS EXPERIMENT EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS NOT sim/adc-power/.
sim/adc-power/ measures POWER per block, averaged over each input
level's own 2 us window -- the right statistic for the ratified
'< 1 mW at 1 MS/s' row. An IR-drop / electromigration read on the
layout's supply geometry (layout/power/, issue #346) needs a
different statistic off the same deck: the WORST INSTANTANEOUS
current the rail is asked to deliver, because that is what a
resistive rail turns into droop. An average understates it by more
than two orders of magnitude here (the CDAC's 72 T-gate legs switch
together), so reusing the power record's numbers would understate
droop by the same factor. sim/README.md's rule is one directory per
distinct claim being tested, not per run -- so this is its own
experiment.
THE NETLIST IS SHARED, NOT COPIED. `netlist` points at
sim/adc-power/testbench/tb_adc_power.spice, the committed,
generator-written deck sim/adc-power/ already records against. This
experiment changes NOTHING about the circuit: same netlist file, same
supplies, same stimulus, same 17 us run. It only adds MIN/AVG `meas`
lines on the same three supply-source branch currents the adc-power
manifest already averages, and reads them over ONE window spanning
every input level rather than five per-level windows -- the worst
instantaneous value is wanted, and it is wanted across all codes.
SIGN CONVENTION. `i(vddX)` is the current INTO the source's positive
terminal, so a source DELIVERING current reads negative; the measure
expressions negate, exactly as sim/adc-power/'s own `p_* = -i*v` do.
The peak DELIVERED current is therefore MIN(i), not MAX(i).
`i_vdd_peak_ua` IS NOT THE SUM OF THE THREE PER-RAIL PEAKS. It is
the peak of the SUM -- `let isum = i(vddc)+i(vddd)+i(vddt)`, measured
as one vector -- because the three blocks do not peak at the same
instant and adding their separate peaks would invent a worst case the
deck never produces. The per-rail peaks are reported beside it so a
consumer can attribute the total.
WHY vddc/vddd/vddt AND NOT vrefs/vcms. In the LAYOUT these three are
one net: adc_block.gds carries a single `vdd` label net (four label
sites, one per sub-block -- layout/erc/). The deck splits them into
three sources only so sim/adc-power/ can attribute power per block.
`vrefs`/`vcms` are separate rails in both views and are NOT part of
the `vdd` island, so they are deliberately excluded here.
WHAT THIS DECK DOES NOT MEASURE, restated from sim/adc-power/'s own
record: the SAR sequencer and output register are DR-0010 rung-1
ideal XSPICE primitives and draw no current, so the sequencer's own
flip-flop and decode current is absent from every number here. The
dominant digital term -- driving the array's 72 T-gate legs -- IS
measured (those drivers are real devices on vddd). A peak read is
therefore a LOWER bound on the real peak, which is the conservative
direction for the sequencer's absence but NOT for a droop verdict
built on it: layout/power/ states this explicitly.
RESOLUTION. The deck's own `tran 1n 17.000u 0 2n` caps the timestep
at 2 ns. A switching spike shorter than that is averaged over the
step it lands in, so every peak below is resolution-limited and is
again a LOWER bound on the true instantaneous peak. Kept at the
deck's own setting deliberately: changing it would make this run
non-comparable with every committed sim/adc-power/ record taken on
the same netlist.
name: adc-rail-current
description: Peak and average current delivered by the vdd rail (vddc + vddd + vddt, the three sources that are one `vdd` net in adc_block.gds), over the full PVT grid. The current model layout/power/'s IR-drop and electromigration read is driven from.
claim: layout/power/ (issue #346) -- the worst instantaneous and the average current the ADC_BLOCK `vdd`/`vss` islands must carry, per PVT point, so a droop/EM verdict on the drawn supply geometry rests on a measured current rather than an assumed one. Not a ratified-spec row: an input to one.
analyses: meas tran icmppk MIN i(vddc) FROM=3000.0n TO=17000.0n
meas tran icdacpk MIN i(vddd) FROM=3000.0n TO=17000.0n
meas tran itrkpk MIN i(vddt) FROM=3000.0n TO=17000.0n
meas tran isumpk MIN isum FROM=3000.0n TO=17000.0n
meas tran icmpav AVG i(vddc) FROM=3000.0n TO=17000.0n
meas tran icdacav AVG i(vddd) FROM=3000.0n TO=17000.0n
meas tran itrkav AVG i(vddt) FROM=3000.0n TO=17000.0n
meas tran isumav AVG isum FROM=3000.0n TO=17000.0n
meas tran vddm FIND v(vddc) AT=1u

i_vdd_peak_ua.description: Peak of i(vddc)+i(vddd)+i(vddt) over the whole five-level conversion span. The bounds are sanity rails, not a ratified budget -- this experiment has no spec row of its own; what it feeds does (layout/power/, DR-0033). The supply-axis spread floor is the harness's own liveness control: switching current scales with the rail it switches, so a supply sweep that showed no spread here would mean the sweep was not reaching the deck.

i_vdd_avg_ua.description: Average of the same sum over the same window. Cross-checkable against sim/adc-power/'s own per-level p_cmp/p_cdac/p_trk averages divided by the supply: this is the same three sources over a window that spans all five input levels instead of one per level.

supply_v.description: The rail the currents above were drawn from, read back off the deck so every current in this record carries the voltage it belongs to. Its 20 % spread across the grid is the +/-10 % supply axis itself.
